summary: The change adds `jobs::provenance` to the live gate (commit-msg hook, Athena's own commits, `athena close`). For each request job a commit closes, it needs a request record received before each reading and the reader invocation the reading names, ended before it. When the base commit is held, defaults.toml there must hash to the reading's defaults hash. A landed job also needs all dispatch fields in job.json, hashes equal to the accepted reading's, a committed brief-producer.md matching brief_sha256, and invocation, verifier and outcome times in the order of a real run. New tests in landing_tests.rs build real git histories for all three §16.2 forgeries and assert Violations whose detail and repair name the evidence and the command that writes it; controls and a genuine landing pass. I ran the athena-gate suite (132 pass), lifecycle (72 pass), refusal_corpus (11), the M24 enforcement-map test and athena-data (157); fmt, clippy and the full suite come from the recorded CI run, and Athena's revert run shows the new tests fail without the fix. The evidence snapshot shows real jobs carry request records, reader invocations under invocations/ and brief-producer.md, and planning runs after dispatched_at, so genuine jobs match the new rules. Docs and changelog state what is detected and the residuals accurately; check_pr_head does not call provenance, as the docs say. Only the five planned files changed. Remaining gaps are minor and documented: pull-request CI does not yet run provenance, so a `--no-verify` commit reaches a pull request unjudged, and consistent forgeries pass without signing.
